title: Pink Lemonade with Raspberry Syrup
summary: Classic lemonade turned pale pink with a quick cooked raspberry syrup and a pinch of salt. The fruit gives the colour, so no food colouring is needed.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring the raspberries, sugar and water to a lively simmer, stirring now and then. Cook for 6-8 minutes (up to 12 minutes from frozen), until the berries have collapsed and the liquid is slightly syrupy.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the salt, which sharpens the fruit. Pour through a fine sieve into the jug, pressing on the pulp, and discard the seeds.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Leave the syrup to cool for 15 minutes. You can also make it ahead and keep it covered in the fridge for up to a week.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir in the lemon juice and cold water. Taste and add more lemon if you like it sharper.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour over ice and float a few thin lemon rounds on top.

tips: Frozen raspberries work just as well as fresh and are often cheaper.
A common mistake is adding the lemon juice to hot syrup, which dulls its flavour; let the syrup cool first.
For a deeper pink, use 300 g raspberries.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
